item.description:
000

TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located well north of the Papahanaumokuakea Marine
National Monument, on Tropical Storm Moke, located a few hundred
miles south of Hilo, Hawaii, and on Tropical Storm Iselle, located
several hundred miles south-southwest of the southern tip of the
Baja California Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&

header WTPZ34 NHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP4.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Iselle are issued under WMO
header WTPZ24 and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP4.

$$

MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...988 MB...29.18 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 33.1 North, longitude 174.7 West. Lala is
moving toward the northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h), and a continued 
slow northwestward motion is expected over the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 175 miles (280 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 47
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 240232
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  47
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

Lala remains a well organized tropical storm despite moving over 
cool waters. The system is maintaining a partial eyewall that wraps 
a little more than halfway around the center, along with 
numerous fragmented outer rainbands. There has been little change in 
the latest satellite intensity estimates, and a blend of the latest 
objective and subjective estimates supports holding the initial 
intensity steady at 55 kt. An ASCAT-C pass from around 21Z was 
helpful in adjusting the 34- and 50-kt wind radii.

The storm is moving slowly northwestward at about 6 kt. An even 
slower northwestward motion is expected during the next few days as 
Lala is forecast to remain located just southwest of a strong 
subtropical ridge, not far from the ridge axis where the steering 
currents are weak. This motion should cause Lala to cross the 
International Date Line around the middle of the week. Although the 
models show the same general theme, there is a fair amount of 
cross-track spread beyond 72 hours. The NHC track forecast is 
similar to the previous one and lies closer to the left side of the 
guidance envelope, near the Google DeepMind, HCCA, and TVCA aids.

Lala is expected to weaken over the next several days as it moves 
over progressively cooler waters, but the weakening trend will 
likely be slow since it is expected to remain in generally low wind 
shear conditions. The GFS and ECMWF models show the storm losing 
organized deep convection around the time it nears the International 
Date Line in a few days. Based on that guidance, the transition to a 
post-tropical cyclone has been moved up to day 4.  Otherwise, this 
intensity forecast is very similar to the previous one and near the 
middle of the guidance envelope.

item.title: Tropical Depression Moke Public Advisory Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
939 
WTPA33 PHFO 240233
TCPCP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Moke Advisory Number  15
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026
 
...MOKE WEAKENS TO A TROPICAL DEPRESSION...
...HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS LIKELY OVER THE BIG ISLAND OF
HAWAII TODAY AND TOMORROW...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.3N 157.3W
ABOUT 335 MI...540 KM SSW OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1003 MB...29.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Moke was
located near latitude 15.3 North, longitude 157.3 West. The
depression is moving toward the west near 14 mph (22 km/h), and this
general motion is expected to continue during the next several 
days. On the forecast track, the center of Moke is expected to pass 
south and southwest of the Big Island of Hawaii tonight, then well 
south of the smaller main Hawaiian Islands tonight and Monday.
 
Recent satellite wind data indicate that maximum sustained winds
are now near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts. Continued
weakening is forecast, and Moke is expected to degenerate to a 
remnant low pressure area by Tuesday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1003 mb (29.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Depression Moke can be found in the
Tropical Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP3 and WMO
header WTPA43 PHFO.
 
WIND: Gusty winds are likely across the Hawaiian Islands during
the next couple of days, especially in areas of high terrain.
 
RAINFALL: Tropical Depression Moke is expected to produce 
additional rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches through Monday across 
the Big Island. Rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches of rain are 
expected on eastern Maui. These rainfall amounts may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides for the windward and 
southeast Big Island, especially in steep terrain and over areas 
that were affected recently by Lala. 

Across western Maui and the remainder of the islands, moisture drawn 
northward from Tropical Depression Moke may bring up to 1 or 2 
inches of rain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Moke, 
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic 
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_cp3.shtml?rainqpf.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Tropical Depression Moke Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
960 
WTPA43 PHFO 240233
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Depression Moke Discussion Number  15
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

Convection associated with Moke has decreased significantly during
the past several hours. The cyclone is now comprised of an exposed
swirl of low- to mid-level clouds, with the remaining convection
now located just south of the Island of Hawaii well to the
northeast of the center. Just-received OSCAT data shows maximum
winds of 25 to maybe 30 kt, and based on this Moke is being
downgraded to a tropical depression.
 
A combination of southwesterly shear and dry air entrainment
should continue to inhibit Moke's ability to develop convection.
The dynamical models forecast the cyclone to keep weakening, with
the system likely to degenerate to a remnant low by 48 h at the
latest and to a trough by 72 h.  The intensity forecast follows
this, and it is possible that Moke will dissipate faster than
currently forecast if significant convection does not re-develop.
 
The initial motion is 275/12 kt.  A strong low- to mid-level
ridge should steer the cyclone generally westward for the remainder
of its life, keeping Moke well south of the main Hawaiian Islands.
The guidance again nudged southward, and the new forecast track is a
little south of the previous track.  Despite this nudge and the
weakening of the cyclone, Moke is still expected to pass close
enough to the Hawaiian Islands to produce a period of gusty winds
and heavy rainfall across portions of the islands during the next
day or two.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rain bands associated with Tropical Depression Moke will continue 
over the Big Island while spreading westward across the remainder of 
the Hawaiian Islands through Monday. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides for the windward and 
southeast Big Island, especially in steep terrain and over areas 
that were affected recently by Lala.
 
2. Although the strongest winds associated with Moke are expected to
pass south of the Hawaiian Islands, strong gusty winds are likely,
particularly in areas within and downslope of higher terrain.
